controls.title: Know and prioritise third parties
controls.statement: Maintain a current inventory of suppliers and service providers, the services and access they provide, and their importance to business operations.
controls.risk: The organisation could depend on an unknown or poorly understood provider whose failure or compromise interrupts critical services.
controls.scope: Suppliers, outsourced services, technology providers, subcontractors and third parties with access to information, systems or facilities.
controls.examine: Reconcile contracts, payments, accounts, network connections and service inventories with the approved third-party register and criticality ratings.
controls.interview: Ask procurement, service and security owners how providers are discovered, assigned owners and prioritised.
controls.test: Sample providers from operational records and confirm each appears in the register with current services, access, owner and criticality.
test_steps: Select third parties from contracts, payments, network access, identity directories, cloud consoles and operational records, plus entries from the supplier register.
Reconcile the samples in both directions and verify service, owner, subcontractors, data, access, critical dependencies, location and exit obligations.
Reperform criticality for selected providers using business impact and concentration or substitutability rather than contract value alone.
Investigate unregistered or stale providers and verify onboarding, review or closure actions are assigned before continued access or service use.
controls.expected: In-scope providers are known, owned and prioritised using current information about their service, access and business importance.

mappings.basis: Requires suppliers to be known and prioritised by criticality.
Requires an approved supplier list for the source control's stated procurement scope.
Requires an inventory of service providers and annual review and update.
Requires the ICT environment inventory to include personnel and third parties.

controls.title: Assess and treat third-party risk
controls.statement: Assess security and continuity risks before engagement and during the relationship, then assign and approve treatment of material and residual risk.
controls.risk: A provider could introduce a serious security or continuity weakness that management never sees or accepts.
controls.scope: Provider selection, due diligence, risk assessment, material changes and recurring review.
controls.examine: Review due diligence, provider risk assessments, identified weaknesses, treatment plans, approvals and reassessments after material changes.
controls.interview: Ask procurement, risk and service owners how supplier threats, access, concentration and outage tolerance affect decisions.
controls.test: Sample higher-risk providers and trace identified risks to controls, accountable owners, deadlines and residual-risk approval.
test_steps: Select prospective, active, changed and higher-risk providers and identify the assessment depth and approval required for each.
Inspect due diligence, independent assurance, control evidence, incident history, data and access model, subcontractors, resilience and applicable obligations.
Reperform selected risk conclusions and trace identified weaknesses to contract controls, treatment owners, dates and residual-risk acceptance.
Verify material service, threat or ownership changes trigger reassessment and that overdue provider actions affect escalation or continued use decisions.
controls.expected: Material provider risks are identified before acceptance, treated and approved by the required authority, then reassessed while the relationship continues.

mappings.basis: Requires supply-chain weaknesses and vulnerabilities to be identified, addressed and documented with controls.
Requires supplier and third-party selection to consider cybersecurity qualifications; the broader risk assessment and treatment remain separate.
Requires consideration of supplier ownership, access and influence, material risk, maximum tolerable outage and risk minimisation for the specified critical components.
Requires secure and verifiable third parties unless business operations require otherwise, with residual risks managed and approved by the CISO.

controls.title: Control third-party access and exit
controls.statement: Limit provider connections and access to approved needs, monitor them during service, and remove accounts, data flows and retained information when the service ends.
controls.risk: A supplier compromise or abandoned provider access could give attackers a trusted route into internal systems and information.
controls.scope: Provider accounts, remote connections, network paths, integrations, data exchanges and service termination.
controls.examine: Inspect approved connection designs, access lists, monitoring, termination checklists, disabled accounts, closed data flows and data disposition records.
controls.interview: Ask service and access owners how provider connectivity is approved, monitored and removed when contracts change or end.
controls.test: Sample active and terminated providers and verify least-access paths, monitoring and complete removal of obsolete access and data flows.
test_steps: Select active, temporary, emergency and terminated provider arrangements and enumerate accounts, network paths, facilities, data exchanges and retained information.
Test a benign authorised action through an active path and confirm least privilege, strong authentication, time limits and monitoring match the contract and approval.
For terminated access, query each target and attempt a safe connection to confirm accounts, keys, routes, tokens and remote tools no longer work.
Verify returned or deleted data and assets, retained copies and unresolved obligations are documented and accepted by the responsible owner.
controls.expected: Provider access follows approved paths while needed and is promptly and completely removed or changed when the relationship changes.

mappings.basis: Advises avoiding direct connections to supplier networks.
Requires secure decommissioning of service providers, including accounts, data flows and enterprise data.
